title: KV cache eviction -> PCIe read amplification probe
body:
Purpose and hypothesis:

This doc captures an ad-hoc investigation into an unexpected source of read traffic over host PCIe during streaming inference with mixed sequence lengths. The hypothesis is that KV-cache eviction churn (caused by mixed-length requests and transient sequence spikes) forces weight/kv blocks off-GPU and back, producing repeated host-GPU DMA reads and increasing PCIe read amplification. In oversubscribed NVSwitch/NVLink fabrics this amplifies queuing and driver re-requests, which shows up as long tail latency for short requests co-located with a small fraction of long sequence streams.

Why this matters:
- We see tail spikes in p95/p99 for short-latency SLAs even when average throughput is fine.
- Root cause candidates previously focused on NCCL or interconnect saturation; this probe isolates host-side read amplification tied to cache eviction and host staging behavior.
- Fixes can be relatively low-risk (eviction policy, prefetching, placement) vs. heavy changes (topology rearrangement).

Experiment summary (what I ran):
- Cluster: 4x A100-80GB (NVSwitch fully connected) + dual-socket hosts, kernel 5.10, CUDA 11.8, NVIDIA driver 535.xx.
- Runtime: production inference binary (build 2024-09-30), NVMM disabled, host-staging enabled for weights > 6GB by default.
- Model: 13B decoder-only, KV cache enabled, quantized 4-bit runtime path.
- Workloads: synthetic mixture generator with 90% short (16 tokens) and 10% long (1024 tokens) streams; arrival Poisson with mean QPS varied 50-350.
- Measurement tools: perf_events for PCIe DMA counters, nvidia-smi dmon (for GPU mem), driver tracing (nvidia-metrics-exporter), runtime logs with timestamps and eviction events, and NCCL trace for collectives.

Observations (raw):
- At 180 QPS mixed workload, p50 latency = 18ms, p95 = 42ms, p99 = 220ms. The p99 aligned with epochs where long-streams entered; otherwise p99 ~ 60ms.
- Perf counters show bursts of PCIe read bytes centered around eviction timestamps in the runtime logs. Bursts were ~1.6-2.2GB per GPU over 100-400ms windows.
- Host DMA descriptor re-queuing count rose by 3-5x during bursts; driver stack trace shows repeated re-reads of the same GPU-address ranges.
- NVSwitch counters show microburst link utilization spikes coincident with PCIe bursts, but sustained NVSwitch utilization remains <25% overall.
- NCCL traces show no synchronous large collectives at those times; collectives present are small (allreduce for bookkeeping).

Root-cause interpretation:
- The eviction policy in the runtime currently evicts LRU KV segments at the end of sequence processing if memory pressure is detected. With mixed-length workloads, long streams extend KV lifetime and cause LRU churn: short requests evicted then immediately re-request the same KV prefixes (for subsequent short-prefix batches), causing the driver to issue host-to-device DMA reads repeatedly.
- Host staging threshold and page-aligned object layout interact: when evicted objects cross staging boundary, re-read is not a single contiguous DMA but multiple scatter-gather requests, increasing descriptor throughput and driver overhead (read amplification).
- NVSwitch is not the bottleneck; the problem is in host<->device movement and the driver's handling of many small scatter reads under memory pressure.

Repro script snippet (how to reproduce locally):
- start runtime with DEBUG_EVICTION=1 and TRACE_DMA=1 env vars.
- run workload generator with: "mixgen --qps 180 --short 16 --long 1024 --mix 90:10 --seed 42"
- tail runtime logs and run: "perf stat -e dma_engine_bytes_read,host_dma_requeues -p <runtime-pid> -- sleep 60"

Quantitative numbers (typical):
- Baseline (no long streams): p99 62ms, PCIe read bytes / 60s = 480MB/GPU.
- Mixed (10% longs at 180 QPS): p99 220ms, PCIe read bytes / 60s = 3.2GB/GPU, host_dma_requeues + 420%.
- After small mitigation (stripe-aligned prefetch + 50ms eviction-grace): p99 78ms, PCIe reads /60s = 520MB/GPU.

Mitigations tried (short experiments):
1) Eviction grace-window (50-200ms): hold recently-freed KV segments for a short tail period.
   - Impact: eliminated repeated immediate re-fetches for short-window bursts, p99 improved dramatically at cost of a small steady GPU mem overhead (~3-5%).
2) Stripe-aligned cache layout: group KV segments into larger contiguous objects aligned to DMA pages so re-reads are larger contiguous DMAs.
   - Impact: reduced descriptor requeues and driver overhead; PCIe bytes similar but fewer packets, p99 improved ~2x vs. no-mitigation.
3) Selective prefetch for predicted short-request hot prefixes: runtime hints based on recent access frequency to keep a small working set pinned.
   - Impact: best p99 reduction when hot-prefix predictions stable; risk if prediction wrong (worse mem pressure).
4) Increase host staging threshold: keep more data resident on GPU (if capacity) to avoid host reads.
   - Impact: effective but not possible for customers with constrained GPU memory budgets.

Longer-term ideas:
- Topology-aware replica placement that pins long-streams to a subset of GPUs to reduce cross-pressure on the working-set of short requests. This is complementary to eviction changes.
- Driver-level batching of small scatter DMA requests when detected, or using large-page pinned buffers for KV objects to reduce descriptor churn. We should evaluate feasibility with infra/driver teams.
- Adaptive eviction that uses recent access heat + sequence-length hints per client token stream to prefer evicting cold prefixes first.
- Telemetry: add a small metric "host_read_amplification" computed as bytes_read / unique_kv_bytes_requested over windows — add to Console traces for customers to correlate p99 with host read amplification.

Actionable next steps (priority):
1) Short: roll out eviction-grace-window (50ms default) to Canary build and run mixed workloads for 72h. Owner: Maya. Linear ticket: RDINF-1214.
2) Medium: implement stripe-aligned layout experiment in runtime branch and benchmark driver counters. Owner: Jonah. Target: RFC by 2024-11-15.
3) Long: follow up with infra/driver to discuss pinned large-page allocations for KV caching; get perf/compatibility guidance. Owner: Priya. Gate: infra meeting Nov week 2.

Notes / open questions:
- Is the observed driver requeue behavior a driver bug or expected behavior given many small scatter DMAs? We should capture a driver trace and escalate if requeue ratio stays >200% under aligned large-object tests.
- Are there customer workloads where holding a small extra GPU fraction (eviction grace) is unacceptable? Provide a config knob and server-side guidance.
- Could NCCL communication patterns accidentally interact with this under different topologies? Our traces show low NCCL contribution here but we should re-run in non-NVSwitch topologies.

Attachments and references:
- Linear: RDINF-1214 (repro steps + logs)
- PR draft: serving-runtime#892 (eviction grace + debug flags)
- Kernel/driver trace snippets saved in internal perf bucket (see linked artifact in Linear ticket)

TL;DR:
Mixed-length streaming inference can cause KV-cache eviction churn that manifests as PCIe read amplification (many small host->device DMA reads). This increases p99 tail latency for otherwise short requests. Short-term mitigation (eviction grace + stripe-aligned caching) yields large p99 improvements with modest memory cost. Next: canary the grace-window and implement aligned-object layout.
